item.text: {"question_id":"5B.9","answer":"During the 2022–2023 energy shock, Scholz’s government took timely, substantially funded measures: diversified gas supply, built LNG import capacity, filled storage, introduced electricity and gas price brakes, and funded relief for households and firms (BATCH-0016-E001; BATCH-0032-E006; BATCH-0016-E018). DIW assessed that the price brakes and relief measures, alongside a mild winter and resilient private action, helped limit the economic disruption; modeled measures supported consumption, but did not prevent a 2023 contraction (BATCH-0034-R12-E001; BATCH-0034-R12-E003). Targeting was mixed: social and energy transfers benefited lower-income households more than higher-income households, while tax relief favored higher earners somewhat more (BATCH-0034-R12-E003; BATCH-0034-R12-E004). Household pressure nevertheless remained substantial: 2023 food prices rose 12.4% and household energy prices 14.0%, while low-income households with limited savings were especially exposed (BATCH-0029-E005; BATCH-0025-E016). Implementation capacity was uneven: the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action did not ensure sufficient staffing to process support applications promptly, jeopardizing disbursement and public acceptance; this finding does not establish Scholz’s personal knowledge or corrective action (BATCH-0003-E011). Related reception-capacity shortages and overcrowding also show broader administrative strain, although accommodation was primarily a state and local responsibility and is not direct evidence about the energy-relief package (BATCH-0011-R04-E014). The government reacted to the November 2023 constitutional ruling by freezing some Climate and Transformation Fund spending, reducing or reconsidering planned expenditure, and proposing revised emergency-budget arrangements, but the underlying fiscal design failure created uncertainty and threatened future investment; most effects were prospective and implementation was incomplete in the cited record (BATCH-0016-E017; BATCH-0035-E001; BATCH-0035-E002). The supplied evidence does not establish systematic monitoring, comprehensive ex-post evaluation, or fully demonstrated corrective learning. Attribution is strongest for the government’s design, funding, and timing of energy measures, while inflation’s decline and economic outcomes also reflected falling energy prices, mild weather, ECB policy, private adaptation, and judicial
